parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized the target as a Node ESM /output/test16.mjs port of yaml.dump(yaml.safe_load(args.a), SafeDumper) with argparse-like --a handling, zero npm external modules, no Python embedding, and executable observation only.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split behavior probing and local implementation search across children while retaining final delivery. One child probed behavior and wrote a wrapper; another attempted a hand-coded parser; the parent wrote and shipped its own wrapper.
parallel.implementation: The submitted implementation manually parsed argv but implemented YAML load and dump by spawning /workspace/dataset/test16_executable from a runtime module, while a separate partial YAML parser and type model remained under /output/lib.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent delivered /output/test16.mjs plus wrapper modules and left extra child-generated YAML parser files in the artifact tree, so final provenance and implementation ownership were mixed.
parallel.verification: Verification compared selected wrapper outputs and CLI cases to the reference executable and reported all compared, but it did not verify a self-contained JavaScript YAML implementation against the zero-external-dependency and observation boundary.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The active artifact violated the local reimplementation boundary by delegating to the reference executable, the partial parser child was interrupted before completion, and official evaluation passed 0 of 147 cases.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same Node ESM /output/test16.mjs target, manual argv behavior, output parity, local imports, and executable-only observation constraints.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single owner kept probing, implementation, vendoring, fixes, and final verification in one timeline, using the local system YAML package as source material for a vendored ESM parser plus custom emitter.
serial.implementation: The serial solution copied the bundled ESM yaml package into /output/vendor/yaml, wrote custom value types, AST loading, PyYAML-style dumping, scalar formatting, CLI parsing, and the entrypoint.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The delivered tree had one coherent entrypoint and module graph with vendor files under /output/vendor/yaml and custom local modules under /output/lib.
serial.verification: The serial actor repeatedly compared Node output against the executable for samples, YAML 1.1 scalars, anchors, aliases, sets, binary values, timestamps, merges, nested collections, and CLI edge cases, then fixed observed mismatches.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial attempt still failed official evaluation overall, passing 43 of 147; its remaining defects appear to be YAML edge coverage rather than an unintegrated or reference-executable wrapper.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final wrapper and the parser child had incompatible end states: one path delegated to the reference executable and the other path was an unfinished local YAML implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor used one local module contract: vendored parser input, custom loader values, dumper output, CLI entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had cross-agent context and provenance ambiguity around what implementation path owned YAML behavior; serial maintained a coherent interface chain.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The active entrypoint used local CLI code but routed YAML transformation through /workspace/dataset/test16_executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial implementation vendored a local ESM YAML parser and wrote custom load, dump, scalar, CLI, and entry modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shipped a reference-executable wrapper; serial built a mostly local JavaScript YAML implementation that covered enough behavior to pass 43 official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parser child wrote partial modules and found a parity issue, then the parent interrupted it before a final result could be returned and integrated.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor kept the same workstream alive through mismatches and fixes instead of cancelling an active implementation source.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost an active local implementation path; serial continued iterating through the analogous mismatch stage to a coherent final artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A child and then the parent both wrote the required /output/test16.mjs path, and child parser files also remained in /output/lib.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial artifact tree had one writer and one module graph: /output/test16.mjs, /output/lib modules, and /output/vendor/yaml files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had competing deliverable provenance and stray partial implementation files, while serial had one consistent final tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent verified byte parity on representative wrapper cases and then accepted the wrapper despite the visible dependency on the reference executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial actor ran broad comparisons, found mismatches, patched them, reran extra checks, and then closed with a local implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel verification showed the wrapper matched selected cases but did not test the essential self-contained JS obligation; serial verification directly drove implementation fixes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spent time waiting on children, timed out waits, interrupted the active parser child, and closed with the already-working wrapper.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run used a longer single-thread budget to continue fixing mismatches until broad checks were clean, though official tests still failed overall.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure cut off the only local-parser path and favored a quick wrapper; serial spent closure budget improving a local implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail: the current completed evaluations report parallel 0 of 147 and serial 43 of 147. The material quality gap is still concrete. Parallel delivered a reference-executable wrapper and interrupted the active local parser child, while serial delivered a coherent vendored-parser and custom-emitter implementation that covered many tested cases.
parallel_contributors: Final artifact delegated YAML behavior to /workspace/dataset/test16_executable rather than self-contained JS.
The active child that was building a local parser was interrupted before it could return a finished implementation.
The output tree had competing entrypoint provenance and extra partial implementation files.
serial_contributors: Serial vendored the local ESM yaml package under /output/vendor/yaml and wrote custom local modules.
Serial repeatedly used observed mismatches to patch dumper, scalar, binary, and CLI behavior before finalizing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial still had incomplete YAML edge coverage, which explains its remaining official failures despite being much closer.
Parallel's selected wrapper may match sampled behavior but is invalid for the requested implementation boundary.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors to a material quality gap, not a discordant pass/fail outcome or exclusive root cause
